plateau.describe: Colorado Plateau: 23 beds, dipping 0.62° to the E; a basement-cored uplift raises them 423 m; an old volcano with 1 basalt flow.
notes: A salt anticline: salt ~723 m into the stack. Once erosion reaches it, groundwater dissolves it and the crest collapses into a long valley. Gravity low.
4 soluble beds (limestone, gypsum, chalk): where exposed, streams lose water into the ground and the rock slowly dissolves.

rockies.describe: Southern Rockies: a granite, gneiss and schist core under 19 beds of cover, turned up into hogbacks along the NW flank; an old volcano with 1 basalt flow.
notes: Regional heat flow ~90 mW/m²; Bouguer gravity low under the range (thick, light crust).
A E-W fault zone of crushed rock wears into a gully and carries groundwater to springs. Resistivity and gravity low.
A N-S fault zone of crushed rock wears into a gully and carries groundwater to springs. Resistivity and gravity low.
3 dikes (NE-SW, NE-SW, NW-SE): hard dark sheets that stand up as walls and dam groundwater. Magnetic highs.
A hydrothermally altered zone 390 m across: soft ochre rock that weathers fast (mineral-belt style). Magnetic low.
A hot spring on the fault: +26°C at the vent, heat flow ~480 mW/m². It melts the snow and keeps the ground unfrozen.
3 soluble beds (limestone, gypsum, chalk): where exposed, streams lose water into the ground and the rock slowly dissolves.

valleyRidge.describe: Valley and Ridge: 12 beds, dipping 0.43° to the SE; tight folds every 980 m, 1401 m high, plunging along their axes; an old volcano with 1 basalt flow.
notes: A N-S thrust fault stacks the beds 842 m: its crushed zone wears into a gully and leaks groundwater. Seismic: repeated reflectors.
A N-S thrust fault stacks the beds 444 m: its crushed zone wears into a gully and leaks groundwater. Seismic: repeated reflectors.
6 sinkhole seeds in the limestone: they dissolve into closed hollows, and streams on bare limestone sink into the ground and come out as cave springs. Microgravity lows over voids.

gulf.describe: Gulf Coastal Plain: 19 beds, dipping 0.20° to the S; an old volcano with 1 basalt flow.
notes: Regional heat flow ~45 mW/m²; kilometres of light sediment and salt below.
A E-W growth fault steps the beds down 74 m toward the sea; water seeps along it. Seismic: thickening beds on the down side.
A salt dome 330 m across, beds ringing it: caprock ~367 m into the stack, then salt that dissolves so the ground sinks into a hollow or lake. Strong gravity low; sulfur in the caprock.
A salt dome 510 m across, beds ringing it: caprock ~446 m into the stack, then salt that dissolves so the ground sinks into a hollow or lake. Strong gravity low; sulfur in the caprock.
5 soluble beds (limestone, gypsum, chalk): where exposed, streams lose water into the ground and the rock slowly dissolves.
